[00:00] Morgan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:10] Daniel (BlueHarbor): Yep, loud and clear.
[00:15] Morgan: Cool. We're, uh, on week three of the pilot, so agenda: go through the lab numbers we ran overnight, look at p50/p95, discuss where gaps are vs your incumbent, and agree next steps. Kevin is going to run through the raw numbers.
[00:27] Kevin (Redwood SE): Thanks. I pulled the two main runs — "shared-pool" which mirrors your current setup and "dedicated-sim" which approximates a reserved slot. Note: some transcription labels maybe off, K-V cache sometimes read as K-V cash in the tool.
[00:45] Kevin: First table, p50: Redwood shared-pool 28ms, incumbent 42ms. p95 Redwood 120ms, incumbent 180ms. These are for 512-token context, batch size 4 steady-state.
[01:05] Priya (BlueHarbor): Wait, 120ms p95 is great... are those numbers from cold start or after warm-up?
[01:12] Kevin: Good Q. Those are warm steady-state after 15 min of continuous traffic. Cold starts — the first 60 seconds — we saw more variance: Redwood 220ms p95 cold; incumbent roughly 260ms. So still better but closer.
[01:30] Daniel: What about throughput? Our baseline needs ~800 requests/min at 200ms avg to meet SLAs. How does Redwood look?
[01:38] Kevin: At batch size 8 we get about 900 rps equivalent in our lab — sorry that's tokens per second confusions — rough throughput aligned. For your workload pattern (spiky), with prefix caching enabled throughput improved ~25% and p95 dropped ~15ms.
[02:00] Markus (BlueHarbor): That prefix caching — is that the same as your KV cache? We have lots of short repeated prompts so that matters.
[02:08] Kevin: Yes, prefix/KV cache. But caveat: when the cache misses happen, we see the larger tail. The incumbent seems to have more aggressive pre-warming for repeated sessions which explains their slightly better cold-window.
[02:25] Priya: Can you show the graphs?
[02:27] Morgan: Yep, Kevin, screen share?
[02:30] Kevin: (screen share noise) Ok, p95 graph here — you can see the spike at minute 0-2 then stabilization. I also added a column with 99th numbers — Redwood 99th hovered at ~310ms in shared-pool, incumbent at ~400ms.
[02:55] Daniel: Hmm. 99th is where our users notice lag. Any ideas why the tail is worse?
[03:02] Kevin: A few possibilities: batching policy interactions, evictions in the KV cache under spiky load, and kernel scheduling on GPU — we saw some context switch events when multiple larger requests land at once. We can tweak batching and kernel flags; small change gave us ~20% tail improvement in earlier runs.
[03:20] Priya: Are those kernel flags something you can run in the dedicated trial?
[03:25] Kevin: Yes, in dedicated or private you get more control over kernel and compilation options. In hosted shared pool we can tune within sandboxed parameters, but dedicated gives a stronger lever.
[03:38] Markus: From a security perspective we need VPC and KMS — can you confirm logs and audit trail availability?
[03:45] Aisha (Redwood CSM): We will provide SOC2 attestation and the KMS integration guide. Audit logs are available via the Console; we can push a sample CSV of event logs as part of the package.
[03:58] Daniel: Also data residency — we need EU region processing for some flows. Is Redwood region available?
[04:05] Morgan: Yes, EU regions are available for Private deployment. For Hosted, we can route to EU region too but if you need a private VPC/on-prem package we can discuss that as an additional offering.
[04:17] Daniel: Pricing? If we move to dedicated slots cost per token swings a lot compared to hosted. We need to balance latency and cost — incumbent is cheaper per token but we pay for their poor tail SLA.
[04:28] Morgan: Understood. We'll draft a dedicated slot quote and include a cost comparison at your projected volume. Also include the cost delta when enabling prefix caching and quantization options.
[04:38] Priya: Quantization — did you test int8? Any quality regressions?
[04:43] Kevin: We tried a quantized path (int8-like) for the model family; small drop in generation quality in niche prompts — we logged delta in the bench sheet. That path reduces p95 by roughly 10-15% and throughput increases ~18%. It's a tradeoff. We'll annotate which prompt categories are sensitive.
[05:03] Daniel: Can you send raw logs? Our infra folks will want to correlate traces.
[05:08] Morgan: Yes — action item for me to share the sheet and raw logs. Kevin, any specific artifacts we should include?
[05:14] Kevin: I'll include the raw timings per request, kernel stack traces for the anomalies, and the harness script. One note: the transcription may show some names wrong — IncumbentCloudAI occasionally abbreviated as I-C-A-I in the files.
[05:30] Priya: On the benchmark methodology, are we aligned on request mix? Our production is 60% short prompts sub-64 tokens, 30% mid, 10% long. The earlier runs were majority mid-length.
[05:42] Kevin: Good catch — the current runs were 50/40/10. We should mirror your 60/30/10. We'll rerun with that distribution and with prefix caching enabled.
[05:55] Daniel: We also want a 6 hour sustained run to see steady-state evictions; the 30-minute run might hide long-term cache thrashing.
[06:03] Kevin: Agreed. We'll schedule two runs: a 30-minute cold-cache run and a 6-hour steady-state run. Expect email with links when complete.
[06:12] Morgan: Regarding the dedicated slot trial — if bench gap remains after tuning, we recommend a 2-week dedicated trial where you can test in your VPC (private) or dedicated hosted slots. Would you prefer hosted dedicated first or private VPC?
[06:25] Daniel: Let's start with hosted dedicated — faster to get up — and then escalate to VPC if needed for compliance.
[06:33] Markus: For SecOps acceptance we'll need the encryption at rest details and an auto-expiring key rotation cadence.
[06:39] Aisha: We'll share the KMS rotation docs and a sample SLA for key rotation.
[06:45] Priya: One more thing — cold-cache p95 variance; is there an option to pre-warm popular prompts?
[06:52] Kevin: Yes, we can pre-populate the KV cache with a set of top-N prefixes or use a warm-up runner. That reduced cold-window in our earlier test by ~40%.
[07:03] Daniel: Great. If you can pre-warm the top 200 prompts for our workload that would be ideal. I'll extract those and send with the prompt set.
[07:10] Morgan: Perfect. Let's confirm deliverables timeline now.
[07:14] Kevin: I'll reproduce the 99th tail with the customer distribution, run the 6-hour with prefix cache, and include kernel traces. Target 2026-06-18 for results.
[07:24] Morgan: I'll send the bench sheet and pricing/dedicated slot quote by 2026-06-13. Aisha will follow up on security docs.
[07:31] Daniel: Sounds good. Anything else?

[07:40] Kevin: Yep, we'll include that.
